EconomyMines.HelpTitle: How does the Mine Report work?
EconomyMines.HelpPurpose: Compute your province's weekly mine report: production, upkeep and miners' salary, ready to share on the forum.
EconomyMines.HelpOverview: Two ways to use this chest: a quick daily report to post on the forum (paste today's text, then click straight on "Entrust it to the scribe", no calculation, no week to pick), or a priced weekly report (steps below).
EconomyMines.HelpStep1: Pick the week you want to process with the arrows at the top of the page — only days within that specific week will be taken into account, even if your pastes contain others.
EconomyMines.HelpStep2: In the game, open the "Management of the mines" tab and copy the whole page text, starting from "Maintenance costs increase..." through to the end of the page.
EconomyMines.HelpStep3: Paste that text into the Mines Commissioner's Log. You can paste the interface several times to complete the data for the selected week: each new paste fills in the data already known, without ever erasing anything.
EconomyMines.HelpStep4: Click "Generate weekly report": it computes the production value, upkeep and net (after salary) for the selected week.

RegistryPage.HelpPurpose: The registry keeps the record of the province's mines, from one office-holder to the next. The Mines Superintendent, the Sheriff, the Trade Minister and the province's leader read it; only the first two record reports in it, from the Mines report.
RegistryPage.HelpOverview: The page has two columns: on the left what helps you decide (the report, then your term), on the right the registry's memory (levels and recorded reports). Nothing is deleted: a replaced report stays visible in the history.
RegistryPage.HelpStep1: Last report, top right: it turns orange if it is two days old or more.
RegistryPage.HelpStep2: Current report: output, value, wages, upkeep and balance of each mine since the start of your term's month (1st month from when you took office, 2nd month from mid-term), up to yesterday. It stays provisional until the month ends. The arrows replace it with a week of your term, recomputed day by day with the prices in force that day; "Current period" brings back the month.
RegistryPage.HelpStep3: Reports for your term: at mid-term and at the end of the term, computed from the reports recorded since you took office. Before the date, the page only says in how many days.
RegistryPage.HelpStep4: Days without data: the days no report covers. A paste contains the game's last 7 days, so a day without a paste is not necessarily lost.
RegistryPage.HelpStep5: Before you took office: the reports recorded by other characters in the 30 days before. This section only appears when there are some.
RegistryPage.HelpStep6: Level history: a rise is an improvement; a drop with no upkeep recorded while the threshold had been reached is shown in red; any other drop is a deliberate choice. A mine whose level changed several times unfolds.

Registry.HelpOverview: Each entry keeps the pasted text, the parsed report, and the prices and miners' wage/hour in force on its date in the province, signed by your character and its office. A report is never deleted: an incorrect report is replaced, and the old one stays visible in the history.

decode.Rules:
The Office des Coffres provides you with a room full of sealed chests. Each chest is locked by a secret combination of five digits (0 to 9). To try to crack one open, submit your combination to the room's organiser.

For each attempt, the chest's mechanism responds:
— 2 points for each digit in the correct position,
— 1 point for each digit present in the combination but in the wrong position.

The maximum score for an attempt is 10 — five digits, all in the right place. If you reach it, the chest opens and we move to the next — you earn a bonus of 10 for cracking the chest!

The overall standings track the points accumulated by each participant. Good luck!

Cookies.Preamble: This page describes how the officedescoffres.creacube.be site uses cookies and local storage technologies in your browser. It complements the {privacyLink}, which covers personal data associated with your account.

Section1.Title: 1. Reminder: non-official tool
Section1.Content: Office des Coffres is a non-official community tool for the game Renaissance Kingdoms, developed voluntarily. It is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by Celsius Online, the game's publisher.

Section3.Title: 3. What we store in your browser
Section3.Intro: No third-party HTTP cookies are set on this site. We use two browser storage mechanisms, both limited to what is strictly necessary:

Preferences.Title: Local storage — Preferences
Preferences.Purpose: remember your interface choices (dark/light theme, French/English language), your default character, and your last inputs in public tools (Watch Report, Mines Report, Stock Report, Animation: Crack the Code, Prize Grid).
Preferences.Data: your chosen theme, language, default character ID, cache of texts you have pasted into public tools, your inventory settings (categories, assignments, order, export options) when you use Stock Report without an account, and the address of your last activity of each Animation type (Crack the Code, Prize Grid) that you created or opened in public mode on this device.
Preferences.Retention: until you clear site data from your browser, or withdraw your consent via the cookies banner.
Preferences.LegalBasis: your consent (GDPR art. 6.1.a, article 129 of the Belgian law of 13 June 2005 on electronic communications, transposing the ePrivacy Directive).
Preferences.IfDecline: the site works normally, but your preferences and drafts are not remembered between visits.

Tokens.Title: Local storage — Authentication tokens
Tokens.Purpose: maintain your connection to your user account during your session.
Tokens.Data: an access token (short-lived) and a refresh token (longer-lived if you check "Stay logged in").
Tokens.Retention: access token valid for 15 minutes; refresh token valid for 12 hours by default or 30 days if you checked "Stay logged in".
Tokens.LegalBasis: these tokens are strictly necessary for the service requested (your login). As such, they are exempt from consent under article 129 of the Belgian law of 13 June 2005 on electronic communications, but documented here for transparency.
Tokens.IfDecline: you cannot stay logged in — you would need to re-authenticate on each action, making usage impractical.

Section4.Title: 4. What we don't do
Items: No audience measurement or behavioral analytics cookies (Google Analytics, Matomo, Plausible, etc.).
No data sharing with third-party services for commercial purposes.
No sale of information to anyone.

Section5.Title: 5. Technical note: HTTP cookies vs local storage
Section5.Content: Technically, this site does not use "cookies" in the classic HTTP sense. It uses the browser's localStorage mechanism to store preferences and authentication tokens. This distinction is purely technical — from the perspective of the GDPR and the Belgian APD (Data Protection Authority), both mechanisms fall under the same information and consent obligations, and are treated identically in this policy. The term "cookies" is used in the consent banner for general understanding.

Section6.Title: 6. Distinction between anonymous visitor and registered user
Section6.Anonymous: Anonymous visitor (no account): only the Preferences storage can be enabled, based on your choice in the cookies banner. Nothing else is stored.
Section6.Registered: Registered user with an account: authentication tokens are added to local storage when you log in. Your account data itself (characters, account preferences) is stored on our server, not in your browser — see {privacyLink}.

Section7.Title: 7. Your rights
Section7.Withdraw: Withdraw consent at any time via the "Manage preferences" button in the navigation. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before withdrawal.
Section7.Erase: Erase stored data: clearing your site data from your browser (Settings → Privacy → Clear data) instantly removes everything stored on the browser side.
Section7.Complaint: Right to lodge a complaint with the {apdLink} if you consider that the processing of your data does not comply with GDPR.

Section8.Title: 8. Changes to this policy
Section8.Content: This policy may be modified to reflect technical or regulatory changes. Any substantial modification will be signaled by a re-opening of the consent banner on your next visit. The date of last modification is indicated at the bottom of this page.

Section9.Title: 9. Contact
Section9.Content: For any question related to this policy or the exercise of your rights, contact: {emailLink}

Data.Intro: For each tool of the Office: what it is for, what you put into it, what is stored, for how long, who sees it, and what happens if you delete your account. The rules that apply to the whole Office (legal bases, rights, security, hosting) are in the {privacyLink}.
Data.Upcoming: Upcoming: this tool is not open yet. What follows describes what it will store as soon as it opens.
Data.Access: Most of the Office's tools work without an account: everything happens in your browser, and the Office keeps nothing. An account becomes necessary as soon as you want the Office to keep what you produce. Finally, a few tools act on behalf of an office in your province: to use the Mine Registry you must hold the Mines Superintendent's or the Sheriff's office and have had it validated in the Office — this is not optional, it is the condition of access.

Account.Title: Account and characters
Account.Text: Your account (email address, password) and your characters (name, town of residence, validation status): what is stored, why, on which legal basis and for how long is described in the {privacyLink} (§3 to §5). This page does not repeat it.

Offices.Title: Declared offices and My province
Offices.Purpose: Have the office your character holds recognised (mayor, or county councillor and their title), so that the tools know who may write on behalf of a function, and keep your province's office history ("My province" page). An account is needed.
Offices.InputLead: Declaring an office is optional — except for the tools that require one.
Offices.Input: You can use the Office without declaring any function. However, a tool that acts on behalf of a province function, such as the Mine Registry, only opens to a declared and validated office.
Offices.InputDetail: You then provide the office (mayor, or county councillor and their title), the city or province, the dates of the term and the link to the public announcement.

MinesReport.Title: Mines report
MinesReport.Purpose: Format the report from the "Management of the mines" tab and compute your mines' weekly report, to share on the game forum. No account is needed.
MinesReport.Input: The text you copy from the "Management of the mines" tab: each mine's state, its hours worked, its output and the resources consumed. It contains no player name.
MinesReport.Stored: Nothing is stored on our servers: the calculation happens in your browser. If you have accepted preference cookies, your browser keeps, for each week, the merged pasted reports, along with the prices and hourly rate you entered, so you find them again at your next paste. Without that consent, nothing is kept.
MinesReport.Duration: In your browser, until you clear the site's data or withdraw your consent to preference cookies, which erases them immediately.
MinesReport.Audience: No one but you: this data does not leave your browser, except what you choose to publish on the game forum.
MinesReport.Deletion: No effect: the Mines report is not tied to any account.

MineRegistry.Title: Mine Registry
MineRegistry.Purpose: Keep a province's mine management record, handed from one office-holder to the next: the Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff save their reports to it, and the Trade Minister and the province's leader (count, duke…) may read them. You must hold one of these offices in the province, and have had it validated in the Office. Without that, the tool is not available. It also holds the province's mine prices, set by the Trade Minister, the Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff.
MineRegistry.Input: The same text as for the Mines report: the contents of the "Management of the mines" tab, copied from the game. For prices: the price of each resource and the hourly wage, with the date they take effect.

Inventory.Title: Stock Report
Inventory.Purpose: Paste the inventory of your character, your city or your province, sort it by category, order it and write up its state for the game forum. The tool works without an account; an account lets you find your settings and your last inventory from one device to another. A city's inventory opens to its acting mayor, a province's to the Trade Minister (who writes it) and to the province's leader (who may read it), with an office validated in the Office.
Inventory.Input: The text of the game's Inventory tab, copied as is, and your settings: categories, item assignments, order, colour, export options. Without an account, everything stays in your browser (if you accepted preferences) and the Office keeps nothing.
Inventory.Deletion: Your inventory settings and the text of your last pasted inventory are linked to your character. They are part of your data export (GDPR Article 20) and are deleted with your character. City and province settings and inventories are linked to the office, not to your account: they are not part of your export and stay in place when you leave office.

InventoryBalance.Title: The Stock Balance
InventoryBalance.Purpose: Compare two inventories copied from the game, the old one and the new one, to see what increased, decreased, disappeared or appeared, and write up the result for the game forum. The tool works without an account. A button lets you load, as the old inventory, the last inventory that Stock Report kept for the chosen level (your character, your city or your province, depending on your office).
InventoryBalance.Input: The text of the game's Inventory tab, copied as is, twice: the old inventory and the current one.
InventoryBalance.Stored: Nothing is stored, neither on our servers nor in your browser: the comparison happens in your browser, and both texts disappear when you leave or reload the page. The load button only re-reads what Stock Report already keeps for you, under the rules described for that tool; it writes nothing.
InventoryBalance.Audience: No one but you: the two texts do not leave your browser, except what you choose to publish on the game forum.

InventoryRegistry.Title: Stock Registry
InventoryRegistry.Purpose: Keep the management memory of a city's or province's stock, handed from one office-holder to the next: the mayor saves the city's inventory, the Trade Minister saves the province's. The province's ruler can view the province's entries. You must hold one of these offices and have it validated in the Office. Without that, the tool is not accessible.
InventoryRegistry.Input: No specific input: the registry records the inventory you have already pasted in the Stock Report. You click 'Save to registry' to create a dated snapshot of that inventory. You may choose a past date (up to 14 days before the start of your term) if the inventory was not saved on the day itself.
InventoryRegistry.Stored: The inventory text, encrypted in the database, with the date, level (city or province) and the author's office. If you replace an existing entry on the same day, the previous author's character name remains visible in the history.
InventoryRegistry.Deletion: Registry entries are linked to the office, not to your account: they are not part of your data export and stay in place when you leave office. The link between the entry and your account is removed.

Watch.Title: Watch Report
Watch.Purpose: Compare two lists of your town's villagers copied from the game, to see who came in and who left, and prepare the forum message. No account is needed.
Watch.Input: Two lists of villagers copied from the game: they contain other players' character names.
Watch.Stored: Nothing is stored on our servers: the comparison happens in your browser. If you have accepted preference cookies, your browser keeps the last list you pasted, to offer it as "yesterday's list" on your next visit. Without that consent, nothing is kept.
Watch.Duration: In your browser, until you clear the site's data or withdraw your consent to preference cookies, which erases them immediately.
Watch.Audience: No one but you: this data does not leave your browser, except what you choose to publish on the game forum.
Watch.Deletion: No effect: the Watch is not tied to any account.

Security.Title: The Guardroom
Security.Purpose: Follow your province's defence: the security trio, validated customs officers and a town's mayor enter defence reports (inhabitants, nicknames met on the road, armies and groups) and keep the province's red and green lists. You need a validated office in the Office, or validated customs officer status.
Security.Input: Pastes copied from the game: the villager list, the road encounters, the armies and groups. They contain other players' character names, entered as they are.
Security.Stored: Each report (one per town per game day), encrypted in the database, with the pasted text, as it is: the villager list (without the preamble), the armies, the groups and the control of the area, and the lines of the visions of the report's day, and the province's red and green lists (nickname, optional reason, date added, author). If you apply to become a customs officer: your status and its dates.
Security.Deletion: Your customs officer status is in your data export. For the lists and reports, the export only shows that you added entries to the lists and entered reports (dates, towns, colour), without their content: no nicknames, no reasons, no reports, which belong to the town and the province, not to your account, and contain too much third-party data. When you delete your account, the link with what you entered is removed; the content stays.

Animation.Title: Animation
Animation.Purpose: Run an activity for the community and share its page on the game forum: Crack the Code (chests sealed by a secret combination that players try to crack) or the Prize Grid (a grid of prizes that is drawn, then chosen cell by cell by players). You can run it without an account (a nickname and a password are enough) or with a character, which then carries everything.
Animation.Input: The activity's name, its location (kingdom, province or city), an organiser nickname and a password in public mode, and, if you wish, an email address, confirmed by a link. Then the activity's content: for Crack the Code, the proposals received and the names of the characters who made them; for the Prize Grid, the prizes and the names of the characters who chose a cell. What is not stored: no password in plain text (it is hashed), no IP address (only a one-way fingerprint, erased on closing), and nothing more than what is listed above.

Map.Title: Kingdoms map
Map.Purpose: Pick a town from the game's reference list of kingdoms, provinces and towns, for instance when creating a character, changing residence or requesting an office. No account is needed.
Map.Stored: No personal data: the map is the same for everyone, and it knows nothing about you.

MineRegistryFields.Text: the prices and wage/hour in force in your province on the report's date, kept with it because they change over time. They come from the province's price table (see below), not from anything you type.

MineRegistryFields.Label: Province and office
MineRegistryFields.Text: the province where you hold your office — not your town of residence —, the office used (Mines Superintendent or Sheriff), and the character who saved the report.

Section3.MinePricesIntro: If you are the Trade Minister, Mines Superintendent or Sheriff of a province and you record or correct that province's mine prices, the Office keeps:

MinePricesFields.Label: The prices
MinePricesFields.Text: the price of each resource and the miners' hourly wage, with the date they take effect. A price stays in force until the next one.

MinePricesFields.Label: The province
MinePricesFields.Text: your office's province, not your city of residence.

MinePricesFields.Label: Who recorded it
MinePricesFields.Text: the character who recorded the price and the one who last corrected it, with the date and time.

Section3.AnimIntro: The Animation module offers activities that you run for the community: Crack the Code (chests sealed by a secret combination) and the Prize Grid (a grid of prizes to draw). Each activity can be played two ways. In private mode, the activity is linked to your character, which carries everything needed: nothing more is asked, and the activity disappears with your character or your account (see §5). In public mode, to create and manage an activity without using a character, the Office stores:

AnimFields.Label: A nickname
AnimFields.Text: the one you choose to be identified as the organiser on the activity's public page — required, so you can be contacted if needed.

AnimFields.Label: A password
AnimFields.Text: chosen by you, stored hashed (never in plain text), to prove you are the organiser for every management action. You can reset it via your confirmed email address, or by requesting a reset from the site administrator.

AnimFields.Label: An email address (optional)
AnimFields.Text: if you provide and confirm it via the link we send you, it lets you reset your own password and be warned each time it is changed; for Crack the Code, it also lets you receive a full report of your activity when it closes. Without a confirmed address, a reset remains possible by contacting the site administrator. An address provided but not confirmed is never used. It is erased when the activity closes.

AnimFields.Label: A fingerprint computed from your IP address
AnimFields.Text: a one-way fingerprint (HMAC-SHA256): it lets us recognise the same connection to check that you are not creating several public activities of the same type at once, but we cannot recover the underlying address from it. It is erased as soon as your activity closes.

Section3.AnimNote: In both modes, the character names you enter — whoever attempted a combination or cracked a chest (Crack the Code), whoever chose a cell (Prize Grid) — are freely typed by you, from what you receive (forum, newsletter, in-game). We do not verify them, and they are not linked to any account.
Section3.AnimActivitiesIntro: Depending on the activity, the Office also stores its content:

AnimActivities.Label: Crack the Code
AnimActivities.Text: the chests, their secret combination (encrypted) and the proposals received.

AnimActivities.Label: Prize Grid
AnimActivities.Text: the grid's dimensions and its prizes (each prize's name and the cell it sits in).

Section3.InventoryIntro: If you use Stock Report, the Office keeps the following. With an account, your inventory settings are stored in the database so that you can find them again from one device to another; without an account, they stay in your browser and the Office keeps nothing.

InventoryFields.Label: Your inventory settings
InventoryFields.Text: custom categories, hidden categories, category order and colour, item-to-category assignments, export and display options. They are not encrypted.

InventoryFields.Label: The inventory text you paste
InventoryFields.Text: encrypted in the database, and readable only by those named in §6.

InventoryFields.Label: Personal inventory
InventoryFields.Text: linked to your character; a single copy, replaced each time you paste; deleted with your character.

InventoryFields.Label: City inventory
InventoryFields.Text: linked to the city where you are the acting mayor; a single copy of the last paste, replaced each time you paste; the inventory may also be saved, at your initiative, as a dated snapshot (Stock Registry), whose history is kept and handed on to your successor.

InventoryFields.Label: County inventory
InventoryFields.Text: linked to the province where you are the Trade Minister; a history is kept: one copy per day, a second paste on the same day replacing the first (which can no longer be viewed, but is kept); the history is handed on to your successor. County inventories are also saved as dated snapshots (Stock Registry).

Section3.InventoryNote: City and province settings and inventories are office data: they stay in place when their author leaves office, only the link to the author is removed. If an inventory is replaced by another officer, the previous author's character name remains visible in the stock registry history, to ensure traceability of office data. No site administration interface lets anyone view your inventories or your settings: this restriction is written into the code, checked automatically at every release, and the source code is public. The publisher nevertheless keeps technical access to the hosting, like any site administrator, and undertakes not to use it to view this data.
Section3.SecurityIntro: The Guardroom (Security module) — if your character is a customs officer, a Constable, a Sergeant, a Captain, a Judge, a Public Prosecutor, a province leader (count, duke…) or a mayor, the Office lets you, depending on your title, view or enter information related to the defence of your province. The Office keeps:

SecurityFields.Label: Your customs officer status
SecurityFields.Text: If you apply to become a customs officer: your character, the town you are attached to and the province, the state of your application (pending, validated, refused, withdrawn), the dates, the level of the decision (Constable or Sergeant; in their absence Captain, leader or mayor; or administrator), the character who decided (kept for traceability, never displayed), the date of your latest report entered — it is used to withdraw access after a long period of inactivity — and the reason access ended. You apply for this role yourself: nobody is registered automatically.

SecurityFields.Label: The red and green lists
SecurityFields.Text: Province-level lists of character names to watch (red) or trusted (green). Each entry contains a freely typed nickname (the character may not have an Office account), an optional reason, the date of addition and the character who added it. These lists colour the nicknames in defence reports: red for the red list, green for the green list. The colour applies from the date of addition, as long as the entry is on the list: reports older than the addition do not carry it. Removing an entry deletes it permanently; the reports then no longer show it, and adding it again later starts from a new date.

SecurityFields.Label: Defence reports
SecurityFields.Text: One report per town per game day, entered by an authorised office-holder (Constable, Sergeant, Captain, the town's mayor or a customs officer) from what they see in-game. It may contain: the list of inhabitants (nickname, reputation, nobility); the nicknames encountered on the road the previous night; the armies and groups present (for an army: its name, its leader and its status text; for a group: its name, all its members and its status text); the text of the "Zone control" section. The text you paste is also kept as it is: the villager list (without the preamble), the armies, the groups and the control of the area, and the lines of the visions of the report's day; the rest of the pasted text is not kept. This information is encrypted server-side; only the lookup axes (province, town, game day, link to the author) are stored in clear text.

Section3.SecurityNote: The character names in the lists and reports — inhabitants, travellers, soldiers — are copied from the game. The Office does not verify them and they are not linked to any account: their presence reflects a surveillance activity carried out within the game, not a judgement by the Office. The people named are not informed one by one; this policy is the information intended for them. No site administration interface can display the lists or the reports: this restriction is written in the code, checked automatically with every release, and the source code is public. The publisher nevertheless keeps technical access to the hosting, like any site administrator; he undertakes not to use it to view them.

Section5.Title: 5. How long we keep your data
Section5.ActiveAccount: Active account: your data is kept as long as your account exists.
Section5.InactiveAccount: Inactive account: after 1 year without login, your account may be automatically deleted, following a notice email to the declared address.
Section5.UnverifiedAccount: Unverified account: if the email address is not confirmed, the account is deleted after 30 days, and no sooner than one week after a reminder sent to that address.
Section5.DeletedAccount: Deleted account: immediate and definitive deletion of the associated personal data (email, hashed password, linked characters).
Section5.TechnicalLogs: Technical logs (server access, application errors): kept for a maximum of 12 months for incident investigation and service security, then erased.
Section5.Mandates: Declared offices: your requests and terms, including ended, rejected or revoked ones with their reason, are kept as long as your account exists. When your character or your account is deleted, everything is erased EXCEPT the history of offices held: your character's name, the office, the province or city, the dates and how the office ended. This information is public in the game; what remains is a pseudonym and a role, and the Office no longer keeps anything linking that pseudonym to you (no email address, no account).
Section5.MineRegistry: Mine Registry: the reports you save are kept with no time limit, because together they form a province's management record, handed from one office-holder to the next. If you delete your character or your account, the report remains, but its link to your account is removed: it keeps its date, its province and the office used, and no longer names any character. We say "the link is removed" rather than "the report is anonymised": the province's office history remains available, and it may allow a date and an office to be matched to a character name. Finally, no report can be deleted, not even by the person who wrote it: an incorrect report is replaced, and the replacement stays visible.
Section5.MinePrices: Mine prices: recorded prices are kept with no time limit, because they are used to compute the province's reports, from one office-holder to the next. You can correct a price while you hold the office, and up to 7 days after your term ends; after that it is locked. Successive price sets form a history and all remain viewable; however, correcting a set replaces its values, and the previous value is not kept. Nobody can delete a price. When your character or account is deleted, the prices stay, but their link to your account is removed: they keep their date and province and no longer name any character. Again, "the link is removed", not "anonymised": the province's office history may let someone match a date to a character's name.
Section5.Animation: Animation (Crack the Code, Prize Grid): in private mode, the activity and its content — the chests and the proposals you entered (Crack the Code), the prizes (Prize Grid) — are kept for as long as you do not delete the activity, the character, or the account that created it — deleting any of those deletes the activity with them, content included. In both modes, an activity with no action for 30 days is automatically closed; in private mode you can reopen it and everything is kept, whereas in public mode this closure is final: no reopening is possible. In public mode, on closing, whether manual or automatic, the fingerprint of your connection, your email address, your password and any pending reset request are erased; for Crack the Code, a report including all proposals received is first sent to your email address if you confirmed one. What stays visible to the community for 5 years after closing: the activity's name, your organiser nickname and the location, plus, for Crack the Code, the chests cracked with the nickname of who found them and the final standings — never the proposals received, which are erased on closing — and, for the Prize Grid, the dimensions, all the prizes and the names of the characters who chose a cell. After that period, the page and the nickname are deleted. To request the removal of a name entered on one of these pages before that period, contact {email}.
Section5.Inventory: Stock Report: your personal settings and inventory are kept as long as your character exists, and deleted with it. A city's or a province's settings and inventory are kept as long as that city or province exists in the game's reference data, and stay in place when their author leaves office. A province's or city's inventory history is kept with no time limit, because it forms the office's management memory, handed from one office-holder to the next. If you delete your character or your account, what concerns a city or a province remains, but its link to your account is removed: we say "the link is removed" rather than "anonymised", as for the Mine Registry.
Section5.Security: The Guardroom: your customs officer status is kept as long as your character exists and deleted with it. The entries of the red and green lists, as long as they have not been removed (a removal deletes them permanently), and the defence reports are kept without any time limit, because they form the province's defence memory: reports are used to compare one day with the next (arrivals and departures) and to hand a follow-up from one office-holder to the next; an expiry date would make these uses inoperable. When your character or your account is deleted, what you entered stays, but the link with your account is removed: we write "the link is removed" and not "anonymised", as for the Mine Registry. The third-party nicknames in the lists and reports are not linked to any account: deleting an account does not remove them.

Section6.Title: 6. Who can access your data
Section6.Editor: The site administrator (see §2), for technical administration, user support and checking your office requests — access limited to the strict minimum.
Section6.NoOneElse: No one else beyond the above. No sharing, no resale, no transmission to third parties, including Celsius Online (publisher of Renaissance Kingdoms), except for a duly notified judicial requisition.
Section6.Hosting: Data is hosted on servers located in the European Union (host: o2switch, France).
Section6.ProvincePlayers: Other players whose character resides in the same province, for that province's office history (character names, offices, dates, how each office ended) — including after your account is deleted, and which they may copy to the game forum. Never your email address, your pending requests, your rejections or the administration's notes.
Section6.MineRegistryHolders: The Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff of the province concerned, who keep that province's Mine Registry, as well as its Trade Minister and its leader (count, duke…), who may read it — including the office-holders who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. That is the registry's very purpose: a province's mines pass from hand to hand, and every office is vacated at each election. Never the other councillors, never a player from another province.
Section6.MinePricesHolders: Mine prices: the province's Trade Minister, Mines Superintendent and Sheriff, who manage them, and its leader (count, duke…), who may read them — including the office-holders who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. The other holders of these three offices also receive, once a day, an email summarising the prices that changed and naming the character who changed them. Never the other councillors, never a player from another province.
Section6.AnimationHolders: Animation (Crack the Code, Prize Grid): an activity's public page is visible to everyone, whether created in private or public mode — that is the point of these tools, shared on the game's forum. It shows the name, the location and the organiser's nickname, plus, for Crack the Code, the chests cracked and the standings; for the Prize Grid, visible from the draw onwards, the cells and, for each chosen cell, the revealed prize and the name of the character who chose it (the contents of unchosen cells stay hidden until closing, when all prizes become visible). Your password is never visible to anyone, not even the site administrator. Your email address, if you confirmed one, is visible to the site administrator in the administration panel — to help you if you forget your password and for the technical administration of the service. Your organiser nickname and, if applicable, the date of the last password reset are also visible there.
Section6.InventoryHolders: Stock Report: your personal inventory, you alone. A city's inventory and settings: the acting mayor of that city, including those who succeed you. A province's inventory and settings, history included: the acting Trade Minister and the province's leader (count, duke…), the latter read-only — including those who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. Never the other councillors, never a player from another city or province, and no site administration interface (see §3).
Section6.SecurityHolders: The Guardroom: the lists and the reports are never public. The security trio (Constable, Sergeant and Captain, in office): read and write, lists and reports, across the whole province; only the Constable and the Sergeant correct a report already entered or enter a past day. Validated customs officers: read and enter the reports of every town in their province, read the lists; write to the lists only if no member of the trio is known to the Office for the province. The mayor: read and enter the reports of their town (of the whole province if also a validated customs officer), read the lists, write under the same condition as customs officers. The Judge: read the lists and add to the red list, never remove. The Public Prosecutor and the province leader (count, duke…): read-only, lists and reports — including those who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. The author of a list entry is visible only to the trio; others see "added by me" on their own entries and nothing on others'. The author of a report is never displayed. Never the other councillors, never a player without a title, and no site administration interface (see §3).

Section7.Title: 7. Your GDPR rights
Section7.Intro: In accordance with articles 15 to 22 of the GDPR, you have the following rights over your personal data at any time:

Rights.Label: Right of access
Rights.Text: obtain confirmation that your data is being processed and receive a copy.

Rights.Label: Right to rectification
Rights.Text: correct inaccurate data about you (email and pseudonym editable from your Profile; other fields on request).

Rights.Label: Right to erasure ("right to be forgotten")
Rights.Text: request the deletion of your account and all associated data.

Rights.Label: Right to restriction of processing
Rights.Text: request the suspension of processing of your data in certain situations.

Rights.Label: Right to object
Rights.Text: object to the processing of your data based on legitimate interest.

Rights.Label: Right to data portability
Rights.Text: receive a copy of your personal data in a common electronic format, to transmit it to another service.

Section7.Complaint: Right to lodge a complaint with the {apdLink} if you consider that the processing of your data does not comply with GDPR.
Section7.HowToExercise: To exercise these rights: contact {email}. A response will be provided within a maximum of one month. Your data can be downloaded and your account can be deleted immediately from your Profile; the email channel remains available as a fallback.
Section7.SecurityThirdParty: Third-party data in the Guardroom: the character names appearing in defence reports and in the red/green lists reflect decisions and observations made in-game by the province's authorised office-holders. The Office records them; it does not make those decisions and does not moderate them. Any challenge to a provincial decision (such as a list entry) is a matter for the game, with the province concerned.

Section8.Title: 8. Security of your data
Section8.Intro: We implement the following technical and organizational measures to protect your data:
Measures: Passwords hashed (never stored in plain text, impossible to reconstruct).
OAuth 2.0 token authentication (Laravel Passport): short-lived access token (15 minutes) and separate refresh token (12 hours or 30 days with "Stay logged in").
Refresh token rotation on each use, with reuse detection (possible compromise signal).
Mandatory email verification before first login.
Administrator access restricted to a single role, manually assigned by the editor.
Section8.BreachNotice: No system being infallible, in the event of a security breach affecting your personal data, you will be notified in accordance with article 34 of the GDPR.
